The Quiet Power of Slow Mornings

Starting the day without a screen changes how the rest of the day unfolds. People who protect their first hour report calmer decisions and better focus across the afternoon, according to several small studies.

The habit itself is simple: wake up, drink water, write three lines on paper, and only then open the phone. Nothing about it requires special equipment or a long routine, which is why it tends to stick.

Why it works

Attention is a limited resource. Spending it on other people's agendas before you have set your own leaves less for the work that matters to you.
